blocks.text: Now use the join in your paper sculpture. Decide where a tab could connect the form to the base. Make and test the join. You can change the position if the real test gives you a reason.
Keep an clear, true record of what you did. It may be the form itself, a clear work-only photo with a note, or a located recording of your action and explanation.

Then look at your drawing record. Under Drawing, say what you tried and what you learnt from it. Under Paper sculpture, do the same for folding, standing or joining. Point to your own evidence for each.

items: Core: use a prepared wide tab and help with the tape backing. Place and test your join. Use the two activity prompts to say your own learning from both art tasks for a verbatim scribe.

Challenge: retain both art tasks and their learning, then explain a useful difference between making a mark and building a form.

blocks.text: BUILD · Art · Trinity Arts Award Explore. Connect The Artist, Organisation And What I Found.
Objective: Use real experience records to explain what you found about an artist and an arts organisation, and check both are evidenced.
Success evidence: Own findings about both real roles, a supported connection or labelled comparison, exact record locations and an honest next action for any gap.
You can explore through looking, listening, asking and trying. Choose a way to take part that works for you. You do not need to share private facts about your life.
We may go to them, they may come in, or we may meet live on screen. The route comes from the current slot card. No meeting is promised by this deck.
40-minute lesson frame. Staff may extend or split the real experience across sessions.

This deck serves Explore Part B, Explore. Part B requires at least one artist AND at least one arts organisation, through live or active experience. Desk research alone fails; archives and prerecorded video are preparation only. Explore has four parts, each a distinct activity. Overall Pass allows ONE Attempted. Any Not Attempted = Below Pass. The whole Explore portfolio has a 10-file cap, organised digitally by part. The three assessment areas are art form knowledge and understanding, creativity, and communication. Results are Pass or Below Pass only. Only an adviser trained at Explore may assess; delivery is through a validated centre. Neither local training nor validation is asserted as confirmed here. Advisers must not write plans, reviews or evidence for pupils. Scribe or record the pupil's own words and check them back unchanged. Core, Extend and Challenge are support routes within Explore and retain the live or active requirement. An evidence locator names the filename plus page, slide or timecode. Read the current PRACTITIONER_SLOT and ORG_SLOT from tools/artsaward/SLOTS.json; no candidate name or date is embedded here. R1 pupils visit, R2 the artist or arts organisation comes in, R3 live remote exchange: all remain unconfirmed until actually arranged. Do not treat a recorded video as a live exchange. Source: tools/artsaward/SPEC.json, Explore and universal rules. This deck consolidates Explore Part B only. It does not replace either required live/active element with a folder check or a classroom model. Use the actual artist and organisation records and check identities against the current slots. A single genuine experience can serve both if the pupil’s exploration of each is clear. If two experiences involved unrelated people and groups, allow a comparison of their arts roles without inventing a working relationship. Missing actual participation must be completed when arranged, with time beyond this lesson if needed. The pupil’s explanation is theirs; do not author it for them. Explaining Part B findings here is a formative learning check, not a claim that the distinct Explore Part D enjoyment/achievement share is complete.

before.title: I Do 2 · connect
before.data-ta1: Accept a comparison when no organisational relationship is evidenced. Do not supply facts to make the pupil’s connection more impressive.

blocks.text: A working link or your comparison?
There are two clear ways to connect the findings. Choose the one your records support.
A working link means the real artist and group did some work together. The source must show that link. Name where it can be found.
A comparison means you have noticed a shared idea or a difference. It is your thought about the two experiences.
You might compare the tools or the space. Or look at how people take part. That does not mean the artist belongs to the group.
Use words that keep the difference clear. Does the record show a real link? Or did you notice a shared idea?
Make a small sketch, use arrows or explain aloud. Keep a detail from each real record beside the link.
If you are unsure, keep it as a question. You do not need to force a connection that the work does not support.

after.title: I Do 2 · connect
after.data-ta1: Accept a comparison when no organisational relationship is evidenced. Do not supply facts to make the pupil’s connection more impressive.

blocks.text: A fact or your own comparison?
Here are two made-up notes for practice.
Artist note: I tried a fold the artist showed.
Group note: I moved a display so people could see the work.
We can compare two jobs. One helps to make art. The other helps people see it.
Can we say the artist works for that group? No. These notes do not show that.
A real source may name a workshop the group ran with that artist. Then we can say they worked together at that workshop. It still does not tell us the artist is on the staff.
Now look at your own two records. What can each one show?
If both name a real shared event, point to that source. If they do not, keep your link as a comparison.
Say what is alike or what differs. Do not add a fact to make a neat story.
Keep a real detail from each record beside your words. If you are unsure, keep a question to ask.

reviewFindings.finding: Artist and arts group questions can overlap. Do not force a unique artist/group bin for an ambiguous question.
reviewFindings.resolution: The new question activity chooses a question against an explicit purpose; real artist and organisation requirements stay separate.

reviewFindings.finding: Predicted paper or print behaviour must not be recorded as the observed result.
reviewFindings.resolution: Both prediction activities distinguish the model reason from the real physical test; retained lab stages require the pupil to use what actually happens.

reviewFindings.finding: A prepared arts-space diagram could look like a claim about a venue.
reviewFindings.resolution: Its picture, caption, questions and transfer label it as a made-up classroom example; no booking or real group role is asserted.

reviewFindings.finding: Taste and personal enjoyment cannot have a model right answer.
reviewFindings.resolution: Checks judge visible details and stated example messages. Pupils choose their own artwork, enjoyment and achievement in the preserved making/sharing stages.

reviewFindings.finding: The source record initially retained a mutable reference to the replacement block.
reviewFindings.resolution: The before block was restored from the fixed git source. All remaining spec changes are enumerated under secondaryChanges; objectives, allocations, time, practical tasks and print choices remain checked.
